stemMd: A real number $x$ satisfies $0<x<10$ and $\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{10-x}=\frac{5}{12}$. What is the greater possible value of $x$?
explanationMd: Combine the fractions using the nonzero denominator x(10−x). Their numerator is (10−x)+x=10, so 10/[x(10−x)]=5/12. Cross-multiplication gives 120=50x−5x², or x²−10x+24=0. Factor as (x−4)(x−6)=0. Both values lie between zero and ten and satisfy the original equation; the greater is 6.
